thread:
priya: quick RFC follow-up 1: proposing a 'gradient rollout' that treats canary fraction as a continuous f(t) and uses deterministic hashing for low-overhead enforcement. jotting tradeoffs + tiny policy sketch.
kyle: +1. short flags: session affinity, drift on rehash, and runtime memory.
priya: affinity modes: sticky-hash (hash(session_id) < f, stable) or drain-next-request. policy picks affinity_mode.
maria: health signals: err_rate_pct, latency_p95_ms, optionally quality_delta. controller computes a configurable composite S.
lia: runtime note: compute decision once per session for streaming/chunked responses; include epoch in hash to allow controlled remaps.
deploy-bot: [bot] recent canary 1778887000 -> peak_frac=0.12 p95_delta=+10ms err_delta=0.25% https://deployments/redwood/1778887000
kyle: abort policy: require M consecutive windows above threshold + cooldown to avoid oscillation. add min_hold_seconds before progressing.
priya: minimal signed policy JSON (sent to runtime): {route,variant,target_frac,smoothing_window_s,affinity_mode,weights,abort_thresholds,min_hold_seconds,cooldown_s,fallback_variant,run_id}.
maria: ops playbook: auto-rollback posts Slack with S(t) snapshot, failing prompts, run_id, and a single-click "pause auto" action.
lia: Console UX: fraction slider + pace presets mapping to smoothing_window_s; timeline overlays f(t) and S(t).
priya: next steps: kyle prototype proto for policy + telemetry; lia mock console; maria short runbook. I'll add this to the RFC addendum. end.
